import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a new column for total spending
data['Total_Spending'] = (data['MntWines'] + data['MntFruits'] + data['MntMeatProducts'] +
                          data['MntFishProducts'] + data['MntSweetProducts'] + data['MntGoldProds'])

# Create a categorical plot to visualize spending by education level
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.boxplot(x='Education', y='Total_Spending', data=data, palette='pastel')

# Add axis labels and title
plt.xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Total Spending by Education Level', fontsize=15)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a new column for total spending
data['Total_Spending'] = (data['MntWines'] + data['MntFruits'] + data['MntMeatProducts'] +
                          data['MntFishProducts'] + data['MntSweetProducts'] + data['MntGoldProds'])

# Create a categorical plot to visualize spending by education level
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.boxplot(x='Education', y='Total_Spending', data=data, palette='pastel')

# Add axis labels and title
plt.xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=12)
plt.title('Total Spending by Education Level', fontsize=15)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.xticks(rotation=45)

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
